tier_rationale: Midland's own full user guide documents every control on the unit (channel/volume knob, wired RJ45 microphone, menu button, PTT) and every function (GMRS channels, NOAA weather, repeater channels, privacy codes, squelch) with no mention anywhere of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, an app, or an account. The only FCC grant found for this model (MMAMXT275, 'MOBILE GMRS TRANSCEIVER') covers only the licensed GMRS/repeater frequencies (462.55-462.725 MHz and 467.55-467.725 MHz) used for the radio's actual transmissions, not a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth band. Per the FCC heuristic, a licensed-service transceiver grant is expected for a radio and is not itself evidence of a cloud connection; there is no cloud connection here at all.
the_unplug_test: There is nothing to unplug. The MXT275 is a vehicle-mounted GMRS two-way radio: turn the knob, pick a channel, press the microphone's push-to-talk button. It has a wired control microphone (RJ45 connector, not wireless), no Wi-Fi, no Bluetooth, no app, and no account of any kind. Every function documented in Midland's own user guide — channel scan, NOAA weather alerts, repeater channels, privacy codes — runs entirely inside the radio. Nothing about it can be revoked, updated against your will, or tied to a vendor server, because it was never connected to one.

sources.supports: Manufacturer's own full user guide: documents every control, menu function and specification of the radio (channels, privacy codes, squelch, repeater use, weather alerts, wired RJ45 microphone) with zero mention of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, an app, or any account anywhere in the document, including the dedicated Specifications section.

Manufacturer's own product page: describes a 'Fully-Integrated Control Microphone' (wired, not the wireless Bluetooth mic Midland sells on its newer MXT295 PRO) and lists price as $199.99 USD; no app or connectivity feature is described.

FCC grant MMAMXT275 (Midland Radio Corporation, 'MOBILE GMRS TRANSCEIVER'), covering only 462.55-462.725 MHz and 467.55-467.725 MHz — the licensed GMRS/repeater transmit frequencies described in the user guide. No Part 15 Wi-Fi/Bluetooth grant exists for this model; the only radio in the device is the GMRS transceiver itself.

open_questions: The schema's `radios` enum (wifi, ble, zigbee, zwave, thread, cellular, lora, nfc, rfid_lf, dect, proprietary_subghz, proprietary_24ghz, ir, unknown) has no value for a licensed-service two-way radio (CB/GMRS/FRS transceiver at 27 MHz or 462-467 MHz). This device's entire function IS its radio transceiver, so tagging `radios: ["unknown"]` understates what is known; a human should consider adding a value such as `gmrs_cb` or `licensed_2way` to the schema. This is a taxonomy gap, not missing evidence — the FCC grant (MMAMXT275) fully documents the actual radio.

Whether the MXT275 requires the owner to hold an FCC GMRS license to legally transmit (it does, per Midland's own FCC Notice in the manual) was confirmed, but this is a legal/regulatory requirement rather than a vendor/account dependency and does not affect the tier.
Current exact street price beyond the manufacturer's listed $199.99 was not cross-checked against retailers.
notes: First CB/GMRS radio record in the catalog. A clean illustration of the FCC sibling heuristic worked as intended: Midland sells this wired-mic model alongside the MXT295 PRO, which explicitly adds a 'Fully-Integrated Wireless Bluetooth Microphone' as its headline feature — the vendor's own marketing draws the exact line this record needed, and the absence of any Bluetooth/Wi-Fi grant for the MXT275 is meaningful because Midland demonstrably would have filed one if the radio had it.
